title: Strengthening Mental Wellness at the Workplace
what_it_is: Strengthening Mental Wellness at the Workplace

sections.label: Employer mental wellness benefits rates
sections.summary: As of 2021, about 47% of Singapore employers provide mental wellness benefits, compared to over 80% in the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As of 2021, only about 47% of Singapore employers provide mental wellness benefits, compared to over 80% in the US.

sections.label: Returns from workplace adjustments
sections.summary: The NCSS Mental Health Toolkit for Employers states each $1 invested in workplace adjustments returns $5.60 on average and reduces medical expenses and retraining costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to the Mental Health Toolkit for Employers published by the National Council of Social Services (NCSS), every $1 invested in workplace adjustments generates an average return of $5.60, reduces average annual medical expenses by 13.3% and increases the average yearly income per person by 6.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Retraining and hiring costs are also reduced, which averages to about $3,650 per employee in Singapore.

sections.label: NVPC Corporate Purpose framework request
sections.summary: The speaker asks NVPC to include this area in its new Corporate Purpose framework for the Company of Good programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask that the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre (NVPC) include this important area in their new framework around Corporate Purpose for the recently-launched new Company of Good programme.

sections.label: iWorkHealth take-up and adoption targets
sections.summary: The speaker asks the present iWorkHealth take-up rate among organisations, MOM's adoption targets, and the percentage of Government Ministries and Statutory Boards that adopted it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What is the present take-up rate of the iWorkHealth tool among organisations and what adoption targets have MOM laid out?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With the Government being the largest employer in Singapore, what percentage of Government Ministries and Statutory Boards have adopted the iWorkhealth tool?

sections.label: Deloitte UK mental health returns
sections.summary: A 2021 Deloitte survey of UK companies found screening gave the highest return from employer mental health interventions, at £6.3 per £1 invested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A 2021 survey by Deloitte among UK companies revealed that the highest rate of returns from employer mental health interventions came from screening, with a return of £6.3 for every £1 invested.

sections.label: Sharing iWorkHealth data across agencies
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOM has shared aggregated iWorkHealth data with other Government agencies so they can recalibrate policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the spirit of a whole-of-Government approach to preventive healthcare, may I also clarify if MOM has shared aggregated data gathered from the iWorkHealth tool with other Government agencies, so that they too can recalibrate policies to better respond to emerging trends from the workplace?

sections.label: CHRO-as-a-service and CET courses
sections.summary: Speaker called for MOM to consider CHRO-as-a-service and for SkillsFuture to push new CET courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: During the MOM Committee of Supply debate in 2022, I called for MOM to consider offering CHRO-as-a-service similar to IMDA's CTO-as-a-service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For companies that are willing and able to address the skills gap, I would like to call for SkillsFuture to push for new Continuing Education and Training (CET) courses.

sections.label: NUS peer support training goal
sections.summary: The goal is around 30% of the NUS workforce trained in peer support skills for critical mass.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The goal is to have around 30% of the NUS workforce trained in peer support skills to have a critical mass to push for cultural change.

sections.label: Funding for EAP consultancy services
sections.summary: Consultants guide employers on mental health data and strategy, with proposed Government funding for EAP providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Consultants will guide employers in making sense of the aggregated data derived from mental health assessments and work with employers to devise a workplace mental health strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I propose that the Government offer funding packages to assist EAP providers in offering consultancy services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Focusing on a smaller pool of EAP providers who meet the required standards will also make it easier to ensure that consultancy and counselling services are delivered consistently, with quality.

sections.label: Calls on Government for employers
sections.summary: Speaker calls on Government to harmonise resources, scale iWorkHealth, expand frameworks, HR systems, training and EAP services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Our employers can and want to take the lead in this pursuit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, I call on the Government to: (a) harmonise the existing resources in a one-stop shop for employers; (b) signal the importance of regular workplace well-being screening by scaling up the adoption of the iWorkHealth tool; (c) expand the Mental Health Framework for employers that systematically maps out the different parts of an employee's well-being journey and identifies the relevant initiatives and key stakeholders to provide support; (d) expand HR systems in-house or as a service to include skillsets that directly enhance workplace well-being; (e) scale up training programmes for employers and employees on peer support, organisational structure, workplace culture and regular check-ins; and (f) expand EAP services to include consultancy on workplace well-being transformation.

sections.label: Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health
sections.summary: Government formed the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being, chaired by Janil Puthucheary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The Government has recently formed the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being, which is chaired by Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary.

sections.label: Employer mental well-being adoption rise
sections.summary: MOM survey shows employers adopting two or more mental well-being initiatives rose from 16.1% in 2019 to 42.5% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Based on MOM's survey on quality workplaces, the percentage of employers who have adopted two or more mental well-being initiatives has more than doubled from 16.1% in 2019 to 42.5% in 2021.

sections.label: iWorkHealth 2022 stress results
sections.summary: The 2022 iWorkHealth results showed one in three employees experienced work stress or burnout.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The 2022 iWorkHealth results showed that one in three employees experienced work stress or burnout.

sections.label: Total WSH mental well-being access
sections.summary: Since mental well-being was added to Total WSH in 2020, over 62,000 employees have access to workshops and over 13,000 attended.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Since mental well-being was incorporated into Total WSH in 2020, more than 62,000 employees have access to Total WSH mental well-being workshops, of which more than 13,000 have attended and benefited from these workshops.

sections.label: SkillsFuture funds mental well-being courses
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Singapore funds mental well-being courses, including the Young NTUC WSQ-certified training programme mentioned by Mr Edward Chia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In addition, SkillsFuture Singapore funds various courses relating to mental well-being which seek to equip individuals, employers, managers and professionals managing workplace mental well-being with an overview of mental wellness, as well as providing information on how they can better support their colleagues and staff in times of mental distress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Mr Edward Chia would be pleased to know that the Young NTUC WSQ-certified training programme that he mentioned is one of the courses funded by SkillsFuture Singapore.

sections.label: Normalising mental health, HPB campaign
sections.summary: HPB launched the 2021 "It's OKAY to Reach Out" campaign to normalise mental health conversations, remove stigma and build awareness and coping skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We need to normalise conversations around mental health and mental well-being and remove any associated stigma.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: This was why HPB launched the "It's OKAY to Reach Out" campaign in 2021 to build awareness and understanding around mental health, empower individuals with coping skills to improve their mental well-being and to reach out for support when they feel overwhelmed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Supporting the mental health and well-being of our workers is key to enabling them to lead a dignified and fulfilling life.
